scope: P1-T03 PostgreSQL storage and P3 durable jobs substrate

environment.roleProof: Integration setup asserted runtime and worker are neither superuser, BYPASSRLS, nor owners of storage tables.
environment.secrets: Loaded from ignored repository .env into process environment; no values or URLs captured.

tdd.reason: Expected RLS/FORCE RLS, business uniqueness, composite FKs, ticket replay, and scheduler fencing statements were absent from the placeholder migration.
Real worker claims returned no rows: SECURITY DEFINER owner remained subject to FORCE RLS.
Actor backfill FK validation could not see referenced actors under FORCE RLS.

verified: runtime and worker role privilege posture
cross-tenant composite FK SQLSTATE 23503 with same-tenant control
approval and execution convergence under concurrent distinct HTTP keys
fair claims with distinct tenant turns

tdd.command: tsc -p temporary storage-only config using pinned workspace dependencies
tdd.note: The temporary config was removed; the root workspace typecheck remains authoritative after integration.

design.migrations: Numbered SQL, SHA-256 checksums, session advisory lock, one transaction per migration.
design.tenantContext: One pg client per transaction; transaction-local tenant and actor settings only.
design.catalog: No global public visibility. provider_catalog and shared_allowlist both require positive per-tenant grants.
design.jobs: One jobs table; separate generation/execution capacity classes; tenant/global/backend leases; fencing on heartbeat, finish, and ledger mutations.
design.workerBoundary: Worker gets opaque scheduling identity from narrow SECURITY DEFINER claim and uses its distinct role under tenant/actor RLS for business rows.

challengedAssumption.assumption: A SECURITY DEFINER function owned by the table owner would automatically read FORCE RLS tables.
challengedAssumption.finding: False. The real DB test returned no claims.
challengedAssumption.resolution: Explicit policy for the fixed migration-role owner on jobs; no worker table-wide cross-tenant SELECT grant.

limitations: This evidence proves the local PostgreSQL substrate, not Medusa remote exactly-once effects.
Scheduler fairness is verified on the local fixture size; it is not a scale benchmark.
The final root workspace typecheck and integration merge remain coordinator-owned.
